"Create a fast-paced, colorful, 3D multiplayer arena battle game inspired by the gameplay style of Brawl Stars, but with original characters, maps, mechanics, and visual identity.

GAME CONCEPT: RIFT ARENA

1. Gameplay

- Top-down / isometric third-person camera.
- Fast-paced multiplayer combat in compact arenas.
- Players choose from a diverse roster of unique characters, each with different weapons, abilities, movement styles, and personalities.
- Characters can be inspired by anything: mythology, futuristic soldiers, animals, monsters, robots, fantasy heroes, or completely original concepts.
- Smooth movement, aiming, shooting, dodging, and combat.

2. THE RIFT TELEPORTATION MECHANIC
This is the game's signature feature.

- Every few seconds, the arena activates a dimensional rift.
- All surviving players are randomly teleported to new positions across the arena.
- Teleportation should happen with a visual warning, glowing portals, energy effects, and sound effects.
- Players must constantly adapt to changing positions.
- Teleportation should create unpredictable encounters, ambushes, escapes, and unexpected fights.
- Players should never feel completely safe in one location.

3. KILL-TO-POWER SYSTEM
Every time a player eliminates an opponent:

- They gain energy and charge a special ability.
- A successful elimination unlocks or activates a powerful super attack.
- Super attacks are character-specific.
- Examples include massive explosions, lightning strikes, temporary invisibility, devastating area attacks, freezing enemies, energy beams, and summoned creatures.
- Super attacks should feel rewarding, powerful, and visually spectacular.
- Players can chain eliminations to build momentum and become increasingly dangerous.

4. CHARACTERS
Create a large and expandable character roster.
Each character must have:

- Unique appearance and personality.
- Primary weapon or attack.
- Special ability.
- Unique super attack.
- Different strengths, weaknesses, and combat strategies.

5. ARENAS
Design colorful, detailed, interactive battle maps with:

- Walls, obstacles, bushes, and destructible objects.
- Strategic hiding places.
- Environmental hazards.
- Teleportation portals and dimensional effects.
- Multiple arena themes, including futuristic cities, ancient temples, alien planets, forests, and underground laboratories.

6. VISUAL STYLE

- High-quality stylized 3D graphics.
- Colorful, cartoon-inspired art direction.
- Expressive characters with exaggerated animations.
- Smooth combat animations and satisfying hit effects.
- Spectacular visual effects for teleportation and super attacks.
- Clean, intuitive mobile-friendly interface.

7. GAME MODES
Include:

- Solo survival: Last player standing.
- Duo battle: Teams of two.
- Team arena: Two teams competing for eliminations.
- Rift Chaos: Frequent teleportations and unpredictable combat.

8. PROGRESSION

- Unlock new characters.
- Upgrade character abilities.
- Earn skins and cosmetic rewards.
- Leaderboards, rankings, and achievements.

IMPORTANT DESIGN PRIORITY:
The game must revolve around two defining mechanics: unpredictable arena-wide teleportation every few seconds and rewarding eliminations with powerful super attacks.

Make the combat addictive, fast, strategic, unpredictable, and fun. Build a playable prototype with functional movement, aiming, attacks, teleportation, character selection, and elimination-based super abilities. Do not create just a visual mockup. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D arena battle prototype called Rift Arena, centered on arena-wide random teleportation and elimination-powered character supers.

## Requirements
- Original characters, arenas, mechanics, visuals, and gameplay inspired by fast-paced arena brawlers.
- Functional movement, aiming, attacks, teleportation, character selection, and elimination-based supers—not just a visual mockup.
- Include solo, duo, team, and chaos modes, plus progression-oriented elements.
- Support phones and tablets with usable touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Implement as a standalone Three.js browser game in `index.html`; bots stand in for multiplayer opponents.
- Prototype uses three selectable runners and mode options in a neon-accented stylized 3D arena.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive game UI, Three.js arena, characters, bots, projectiles, and combat logic.
- Added rift warnings and teleportation, character-specific supers, eliminations, dash, destructible crates, pause/settings, and round results.
- Added keyboard/mouse and touch-control wiring.
- Fixed undefined `worldAim()`, undeclared `color` in `useSuper()`, and team-mode setup/AI behavior.
- JavaScript module syntax check passes; opened the game in Playwright and captured a desktop menu screenshot.

- Exercise character/mode selection, movement, aiming, combat, rifts, supers, and touch controls in-browser.
- Review requested scope against implementation, especially progression and environment variety/hazards.

- (none)

1. Click through a complete round and verify gameplay, team-mode win conditions, rifts, and supers.
2. Test the mobile layout and touch controls; inspect screenshots for layout issues.
3. Address any runtime/gameplay defects, then summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and UI.
- `screenshots/rift-menu.png`: Captured desktop menu screenshot.

## Objective
- Complete and validate Rift Arena, a playable mobile-friendly 3D arena brawler prototype with teleportation, elimination-powered supers, multiple modes, and progression-oriented elements.

## Requirements
- Original characters, arenas, mechanics, visuals, and gameplay inspired by fast-paced arena brawlers.
- Functional movement, aiming, attacks, teleportation, character selection, and elimination-based supers.
- Include solo, duo, team, and chaos modes, plus progression-oriented elements.
- Support phones and tablets with usable touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Implement as a standalone Three.js browser game in `index.html`; bots stand in for multiplayer opponents.
- Prototype uses three selectable runners and mode options in a neon-accented stylized 3D arena.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive game UI, Three.js arena, characters, bots, projectiles, and combat logic.
- Added rift warnings and teleportation, character-specific supers, eliminations, dash, destructible crates, pause/settings, and round results.
- Added keyboard/mouse and touch-control wiring.
- Fixed `worldAim()`, the undeclared `color` in `useSuper()`, and team-mode setup/AI behavior.
- JavaScript module syntax check passes; game loads in Playwright and a desktop menu screenshot exists.

### Active
- Fix menu click interception: Playwright reports the canvas intercepts clicks on `#startBtn`. Recent CSS `z-index` changes did not take effect; inspect/fix the stylesheet, then retest.
- Exercise a complete round, modes, combat, rifts, supers, and touch controls.
- Review requested scope, especially progression and environment variety/hazards.

### Blocked
- Browser-driven gameplay testing is blocked by the menu button being unclickable due to canvas interception.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the CSS around `#vignette` in `index.html`; ensure its rule closes correctly, then verify the `#game`, `#hud`, and overlay stacking styles are parsed and applied.
2. Reload the page and use Playwright to enter a round and check for runtime/gameplay defects.
3. Test mobile layout and touch controls, inspect screenshots, and summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and UI; includes recent team logic and CSS stacking changes.
- `screenshots/rift-menu.png`: Captured desktop menu screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project contains untracked starter/support files.
- Three.js is imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Playwright reports `canvas` intercepting clicks on `#startBtn`; recent z-index edits appear unparsed or ineffective. Console also reports a missing `favicon.ico` (404) and SwiftShader rendering warnings.

## Objective
- Complete and validate Rift Arena, a playable mobile-friendly 3D arena brawler prototype with teleportation, elimination-powered supers, multiple modes, and progression-oriented elements.

## Requirements
- Original characters, arenas, mechanics, visuals, and gameplay inspired by fast-paced arena brawlers.
- Functional movement, aiming, attacks, teleportation, character selection, and elimination-based supers.
- Include solo, duo, team, and chaos modes, plus progression-oriented elements.
- Support phones and tablets with usable touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Implement as a standalone Three.js browser game in `index.html`; bots stand in for multiplayer opponents.
- Prototype uses three selectable runners and mode options in a neon-accented stylized 3D arena.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive game UI, Three.js arena, characters, bots, projectiles, and combat logic.
- Added rift warnings and teleportation, character-specific supers, eliminations, dash, destructible crates, pause/settings, and round results.
- Added keyboard/mouse and touch-control wiring.
- Fixed `worldAim()`, undeclared `color` in `useSuper()`, and team-mode setup/AI behavior.
- Fixed menu click interception by closing the missing parenthesis in the `#vignette` CSS `linear-gradient`; stylesheet now parses `#hud` and overlay rules, and the start button works.
- Playwright successfully entered a round; `#intro` changed to `hidden`.

### Active
- Exercise a complete round, modes, combat, rifts, supers, and touch controls.
- Review requested scope, especially progression and environment variety/hazards.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test gameplay through a full round, including combat, rifts, supers, and mode outcomes.
2. Test mobile layout and touch controls; inspect screenshots and console errors.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and UI; includes the CSS parsing fix and recent team logic.
- `screenshots/rift-menu.png`: Captured desktop menu screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project includes untracked starter/support files.
- Three.js is imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser testing used `playwright-cli`; menu start succeeded after the CSS fix.
